preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 0 and x <= 2**31 for x in [int(stdin.split()[0]), int(stdin.split()[1]), int(stdin.split()[2])])
preconditions.description: The input consists of three non-negative integers a, b, c (0 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 2³¹) representing the counts of red, green, and blue pixels, respectively.
The total number of pixels is at least one (a + b + c > 0).

postconditions.description: The output is either -1 (impossible to achieve peace) or a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of fights required.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == -1 if (a + b + c) % 3 != 0 else int(stdout.strip()) >= 0
postconditions.description: If the total number of pixels (a + b + c) is not divisible by 3, the output is -1 (impossible to achieve peace). Otherwise, the output is the minimum number of fights required.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == 0 if (a == b == c) else int(stdout.strip()) >= 0
postconditions.description: If the counts of all three colors are already equal (a == b == c), the output is 0 (no fights needed). Otherwise, the output is the minimum number of fights required.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == (a + b + c - max(a, b, c) * 2) if (a + b + c) % 3 == 0 else False
postconditions.description: If the total number of pixels is divisible by 3, the minimum number of fights is (a + b + c - 2 * max(a, b, c)). This is derived from the invariant that the difference between the largest and smallest counts must be eliminated through fights.
